name: NY-14
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+19 partisan lean makes the district structurally Democratic
Ocasio-Cortez holds a roughly $16M-to-$31K cash-on-hand advantage over Hysenaj
No outside spending opposes the incumbent and prediction markets price about 97% Democratic

model.rationale: The district's 19-point Democratic lean, combined with the incumbent's roughly 95-to-1 cash advantage and the complete absence of outside spending against her, leaves the Republican nominee without a visible path; prediction markets agree at about 97 percent Democratic.
model.watch: With no polling in the race, an unexpected scandal, major outside intervention, or severe turnout collapse are the only developments that could meaningfully narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New York's 14th District carries a 19-point Democratic lean, and incumbent Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is seeking re-election with advantages on nearly every measurable front. She has raised more than $32 million and holds about $16 million on hand, while Republican Diamant Hysenaj has raised roughly $343,000 with about $31,000 available. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and prediction markets price her win probability at about 97 percent.

No public general-election polling is available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the stark resource gap. Those fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the high twenties. The Republican nominee lacks the money or outside support to alter the race's basic structure, making an upset extremely unlikely absent something unexpected.
